The evidence collector's join from registry rows to supervisord programs now also reads the manifest form of a program's registration line (`forward_port.py --manifest <app.toml> --url <url>`, with no `--name`), which every built-in app and the build-app scaffold write from phase 1 of the workspace app model on: such a call registers under the block's own program name. The `--name` form keeps working, and a block may mix both. A call's flags end at the shell chain operator that leads to the next command (`&&`, `;`, or `||`), so a `--name` on the app's own start command is never read as the registration's. The README's delivered-app section describes the join the same way.

The evidence collector's test fixtures show the terminal program as `terminal-app` (phase 3 of the workspace app model replaced `run_ttyd.sh` with a Python package whose entry point registers from inside the process), which is the same "registers from inside the program it runs" case the fixture stood for before.

The evidence collector's test fixtures show the files program as `files-app` too (phase 4 of the workspace app model made the file viewer a Python package whose entry point registers from inside the process and runs dufs as its child), so `files` joins the terminal in the fixtures' set of self-registered template apps rather than the set the config itself registers.

Phase 6 of the workspace app model (chat as a document): the test fixtures list `chat` among the template apps the registry half sees (`SELF_REGISTERED_APPS`). The chat app registers from inside the program it runs, so the evidence collector's config join never names it and the registry snapshot is what carries the `chat` row.

Phase 10 of the workspace app model (the chat app): every bridged call (`/api/claude-auth/...`, `/api/agents/create-chat`, `/api/agents`, the sends and the events) targets the workspace's chat app, which runs as its own program at its own port. The URL is read from the workspace's registry (`data/.state/apps.toml`, the row named `chat`) inside the same bridged exec as the curl, with `http://127.0.0.1:8010` as the fallback for a workspace whose registry has no row yet; `WORKSPACE_SYSTEM_INTERFACE` is gone. The test fixtures' template supervisord shows `[program:chat]` running `chat-app`, a self-registering program like the terminal.
